indicators.note: to entertain guests is to hold them inside your home, so the word for good holds the commercial

explanation.surface: A decent person hosting an advertisement they then walk away from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' looks like deserted, but here it means dissolute, wildly self-indulgent; it sits at the end, away from the wordplay it seems to describe.
explanation.definitionFit: A less common sense: an abandoned life has cast off all restraint, which is what decadent describes.

definitions.meaning: verb: to shorten or reduce, as wages or a tail

explanation.surface: A gardener pruning a big-leaved plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one gardening instruction, but it splits into two meanings of DOCK: to cut, and the weed whose leaves are rubbed on nettle stings.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to dock pay or a tail is to cut it short, and dock is a weed named for its broad leaves.

clue.text: Learner after opportunity in part of church

indicators.note: 'after' places the learner's letter behind the opportunity, so it comes last

parts.note: L = learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A trainee seizing an opening while inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is read in reverse order of the answer: the opportunity is written first even though the learner is named first.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the chancel is the part of a church around the altar, where clergy and choir sit.

indicators.note: an unusual version of TREAT is its letters in a different order

explanation.surface: A show in which devils are given an odd reward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' at the front reads as a noun, a performance, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: to show how something works is to display it for others.

clue.text: Family member, one scratching head with expression of relief

indicators.note: scratching out the head of ONE removes its first letter

parts.note: the word you sigh when relieved

explanation.surface: A relative puzzled, scratching their head, then sighing with relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scratching head' pictures someone puzzled; here it means the head letter is scratched out.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a sibling's son is one particular member of your family.

clue.text: Pen exclusive news item, not the first

indicators.note: the item is kept but without its first letter

parts.note: a story one paper has before the others

explanation.surface: A journalist writing an exclusive, though not the first to break it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like a verb for writing the story; it is the noun, an enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by type: a pen is any enclosure for animals, and a hen house is one kind.

indicators.note: the answer is taken from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A final note arriving from a menacing mobster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last letter' reads like a final piece of correspondence; it is the last letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: omega ends the Greek alphabet, as in 'alpha and omega'.

clue.text: Puritan at one time forgetting old wariness

indicators.note: what is forgotten is left out, so the old letter goes missing from 'at one time'

parts.note: O = old, as in OT for Old Testament; removed from ONCE

explanation.surface: A strict moralist who once was cautious but has let it slip.
explanation.walkthrough: Puritan has a capital only because it starts the clue; the historical Puritans are a distraction from the plain prude.
explanation.definitionFit: Near synonym: prudence is careful forethought, and wariness is caution against risk.

clue.text: Person who's reticent about one allegation

indicators.note: 'about' in its sense of around: the reticent person goes round the one

parts.note: someone who clams up is a clam

explanation.surface: A tight-lipped person staying quiet about an accusation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' reads as 'concerning' in the surface; in the wordplay it means around.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an allegation is an assertion not yet proved.

clue.text: Dish you put on a table

indicators.note: in an across answer, 'put on' means added after, so you follows a

parts.note: U = you, as in text messages

explanation.surface: Someone told to set a dish down on the dining table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Table' is not furniture here but tableland, a flat-topped stretch of high ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Geographic sense: a table, or tableland, is an area of high flat ground.

definitions.meaning: verb: to take for your own use

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are also pronounced differently: the adjective ends '-it', the verb '-ate'.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the adjective means proper or fitting, and the verb means to seize for oneself.

indicators.note: 'with' means alongside, so the trick sits next to the model

explanation.surface: Weighing up a scam involving a fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' suggests a person on a catwalk; it is a pattern to copy.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to think about something at length is to consider or ponder it.

indicators.note: a flag waving moves about, as the letters do

explanation.surface: A thankful patriot waving the real flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waving' fits the flag so naturally that it hides its job as the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: someone appreciative of a kindness feels thankful for it.

indicators.note: a strange TALE has its letters out of order

parts.note: re = on, concerning, as in memo headings

explanation.surface: A reporter filing a piece about an odd story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report on' reads as one phrase; the split falls between them, with 'on' starting the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: to report events is to tell or recount them.

clue.text: Universal subject primarily covered by comedian

indicators.note: take the first letter of 'subject'
the comedian covers it, wrapping round the letter

explanation.surface: A comedian tackling a topic everyone relates to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Universal subject' reads like a theme with broad appeal; 'Universal' alone is the definition, in its literal sense of the universe.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal sense: universal as in of the universe, the cosmos.

explanation.surface: An elderly fellow who got by.
explanation.walkthrough: The commas make it look like a description of the man; they are only surface punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to have coped with something is to have got by despite difficulty.

indicators.note: 'and' simply adds the article after the looking

explanation.surface: Someone reading a newspaper article and getting angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' reads as a piece of journalism; it is the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to fume is to simmer with anger that is barely held in.

clue.text: Solid doctor working after theatre bombed

indicators.note: a show that bombed was a disaster, so THEATRE falls apart
the doctor and working follow the rearranged theatre

parts.note: on = working, as a switched-on machine

explanation.surface: A dependable physician back at work after a show flopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solid' looks like praise for the doctor; it is the noun, a three-dimensional shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: in geometry a solid is any 3D shape, and this one has four triangular faces.

indicators.note: gnarled means twisted, so ROOTS is twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: An old tree's twisted roots and trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole surface is about a tree, but 'trunk' is the human body without head and limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomical sense: the trunk is the body minus head and limbs.

indicators.note: what reaches the ear, not the eye, counts: the word is judged by its sound

explanation.surface: Standing naked before a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' suggests a court session; it signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: if you can't stand something, you can't tolerate it.

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the reference runs backwards

parts.note: ref = reference, as in a letter heading
an opening for air or feeling

explanation.surface: A glowing testimonial about a shop outlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' first suggests one word going round another; here it only turns the first piece around.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: fervent means burning with feeling, from Latin for boiling.

clue.text: Come into conflict, having no time for point of view

indicators.note: having no time means the letter for time is absent

parts.note: to tangle with someone is to fight them

explanation.surface: Two people clashing because one won't make time for the other's opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having no time for' reads as dismissing an opinion; the 'for' belongs to the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: an angle is the slant from which you view a question.

clue.text: Plunder left and returned as well

indicators.note: what is returned comes back the other way

explanation.surface: Raiders who grabbed goods, left, and came back for more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' and 'returned' look like the raiders' comings and goings; they are L and a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as nouns: plunder is goods taken by force.

indicators.note: whatever carries something holds it inside

parts.note: an end is an object, an aim

explanation.surface: Postponing the return of something carried back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' is the sports position, as in a full-back; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: in football and hockey a back is one kind of defensive player.
